# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by `make config-docs` from config/variables.d/*.yml. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every lever of the cabinet is a variable declared in `config/variables.d/<area>.yml` (name, type, default, range, description, consumers), like Terraform's `variables.tf`. The defaults are the neutral, community values; you override what you need and nothing else.

Precedence, low to high: declared default, `config/targets/<target>.yml` (vm), your local file, the command line.

- Your local file is `$HK_CONFIG`, else `config/local.yml` (git-ignored), else `personal/config/local.yml` (EDITION=personal). Start from `config/local.example.yml`.
- Command line: `make deploy hk_ssh_user=me`, or `SET`-style via the env `HK_SET="hk_a=1 hk_b=2"`.
- `make config-check` validates everything (unknown names get a did-you-mean hint) and runs before every deploy; `make config` shows each effective value and where it came from.
- Secrets never go in config; a variable only says where a secret lives (a Keychain item name).
- A variable with targets `cabinet` does not exist for the VM, and the other way round.

## achievements

### `hk_cheevos_enable`

Turn RetroAchievements on in RetroArch (cheevos_enable) and flycast ([achievements] Enabled).

- Type: `bool`
- Default: `false`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/retroarch122`, `ansible/roles/dreamcast`

### `hk_cheevos_hardcore`

Hardcore mode (RetroArch cheevos_hardcore_mode_enable, flycast HardcoreMode): no save-state loading, rewind, slow motion or cheats; unlocks count as hardcore and leaderboards work. Turning it on restarts a running game.

- Type: `bool`
- Default: `true`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/retroarch122`, `ansible/roles/dreamcast`

### `hk_cheevos_hardcore_by_core`

Per-core exceptions to hk_cheevos_hardcore, as {<RetroArch core folder name>: true|false} (the folder under config/, e.g. "PCSX-ReARMed: false" for softcore on PlayStation). Written into that core's override config/<core>/<core>.cfg. Mupen64Plus-Next is refused: its override is a whole-file copy (retroarch122). Not used by flycast (that one follows hk_cheevos_hardcore).

- Type: `map`
- Default: `{}`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/retroarch122`

### `hk_cheevos_keychain`

Name of the macOS Keychain item that holds your RetroAchievements login token (not your password). bin/deploy reads it at deploy time (COIN_DOJO_CHEEVOS_TOKEN overrides it). Empty = no token is written; log in from the RetroArch menu instead.

- Type: `str`
- Default: (empty)
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/bin/deploy`

### `hk_cheevos_user`

Your RetroAchievements user name (RetroArch cheevos_username, flycast UserName). Empty = none written. Set it in your local config only.

- Type: `str`
- Default: (empty)
- Pattern: `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,32}`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/retroarch122`, `ansible/roles/dreamcast`

### `hk_cheevos_web_keychain`

Name of the macOS Keychain item that holds your RetroAchievements Web API key (retroachievements.org, Settings, Keys), for the TROPHIES page (#176). bin/deploy reads it at deploy time (COIN_DOJO_CHEEVOS_WEB_KEY overrides it) into a 0600 file on the cabinet. Empty = the TROPHIES page shows how to connect.

- Type: `str`
- Default: (empty)
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/bin/deploy`

### `hk_trophies_carousel`

Also show TROPHIES as an entry on the main carousel (#176). Off by default (the maintainer 2026-11-17): tap LP on the main menu opens the same page as an overlay (#177), which needs only RetroAchievements and a user.

- Type: `bool`
- Default: `false`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/esde_collections`

## attract

### `hk_attract_controls`

Let the player start attract mode by hand (ES-DE ScreensaverControls; Short = "x" on the system carousel).

- Type: `bool`
- Default: `true`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/cabinet_tweaks`

### `hk_attract_timer_ms`

Idle time in milliseconds before attract mode starts by itself (ES-DE ScreensaverTimer). 600000 is 10 minutes (the maintainer 2026-11-15; it was 1 hour). It must not take over during play or tests. 0 turns the automatic start off.

- Type: `int`
- Default: `600000`
- Range: 0 to 86400000
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/cabinet_tweaks`

### `hk_attract_type`

What attract mode shows (ES-DE ScreensaverType).

- Type: `enum`
- Default: `video`
- Allowed: `dim`, `black`, `slideshow`, `video`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/cabinet_tweaks`

## collections

### `hk_must_play_genre_min_stars`

MUST PLAY GENRES shows every game rated at least this many stars (0-5, the scraped rating), one folder per genre (#182). Needs `must-play-genres` in hk_virtual_systems.

- Type: `float`
- Default: `4.5`
- Range: 0 to 5
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/esde_collections`
- Also sets the Ansible variable: `esde_collections_must_play_genre_min`

### `hk_must_play_top`

MUST PLAY shows the best-rated this-many games of each system (#182; the maintainer 2026-11-17: at least 20 or 30). Ties go to your Cabinet Picks, unrated games come last. A system with fewer games shows them all.

- Type: `int`
- Default: `25`
- Range: 5 to 100
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/esde_collections`
- Also sets the Ansible variable: `esde_collections_must_play_top`

### `hk_nested_args`

Extra flags for `collgen.py nested` in the esde_collections role (for example `["--min-decade", "1"]`).

- Type: `list` (items: str)
- Default: `[]`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/esde_collections`
- Also sets the Ansible variable: `esde_collections_nested_args`

### `hk_virtual_systems`

Slugs of the generated (virtual) systems: their gamelists are built by the deploy, never edited or copied, and every reader of a gamelists folder skips them. The slug is also the theme badge name. All but `fightcade`, `trophies`, `settings` and `quit` are built by `collgen.py nested` (carousel order = list order, title = the slug in capitals); those four are one-entry tool systems (TROPHIES #176, SETTINGS, FIGHTCADE and QUIT TO MAIN MENU #214), built only when their app is installed. Single source: scripts read it through `skills/collections/nested.py` (env HK_VIRTUAL_SYSTEMS as JSON, else `virtual_systems.json` beside it, which the role writes next to the shipped tools; else this file in a checkout).

- Type: `list` (items: str)
- Default: `["must-play", "must-play-genres", "genres", "series", "decades", "systems", "fightcade", "trophies", "settings", "quit"]`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `skills/collections/nested.py`, `skills/controls/controls.py`, `ansible/roles/esde_collections`
- Also sets the Ansible variable: `esde_virtual_systems`

## dev

### `hk_forge_bot_keychain`

Name of the macOS Keychain item with the ticket bot's API token (comments and labels appear as that user). FORGEJO_TOKEN overrides it. Empty = only FORGEJO_TOKEN.

- Type: `str`
- Default: (empty)
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `tools/tickets.py`

### `hk_forge_keychain`

Name of the macOS Keychain item with the forge ADMIN token (the one that may create releases, tools/release.py; tickets only use it with TICKETS_ADMIN_FALLBACK=1). The value never goes in config; FORGEJO_TOKEN overrides it. Empty = only FORGEJO_TOKEN.

- Type: `str`
- Default: (empty)
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `tools/release.py`, `tools/tickets.py`

### `hk_forge_repo`

The repository on that forge as `owner/name` (tickets are its issues, releases its releases). Empty = no forge.

- Type: `str`
- Default: (empty)
- Pattern: `|[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `tools/tickets.py`, `tools/release.py`, `tools/changelog.py`
- Example: `alice/coin-dojo`

### `hk_forge_url`

Base URL of your Forgejo (or Gitea) server, no trailing slash (`http://forge.lan:3000`). Used by tools/tickets.py, tools/release.py and the compare links of tools/changelog.py. Empty = no forge: those tools stop and say so.

- Type: `str`
- Default: (empty)
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `tools/tickets.py`, `tools/release.py`, `tools/changelog.py`
- Example: `http://forge.lan:3000`

### `hk_forge_user`

Account name of that admin Keychain item (`security -a`). Empty = any account.

- Type: `str`
- Default: (empty)
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `tools/tickets.py`

### `hk_stock_image`

Path of YOUR stock card image (a backup of your own cabinet's card) that skills/local-preview/preview.sh renders when you pass no argument. Nothing ships it. Empty = pass the image as the argument. Old name hk_iconic_image (#240) still works in a local file.

- Type: `str`
- Default: (empty)
- Old name, still read: `hk_iconic_image`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `skills/local-preview/preview.sh`

### `hk_worktree_dir`

Folder for the maintainer's worktrees (`~` is this Mac's home).

- Type: `path`
- Default: `~/coin-dojo-wt`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `tools/wt`, `tools/housekeeping.sh`

## display

### `hk_kernel_4k`

Boot the 4 KB-page kernel (`kernel=kernel8.img` under [all] in /boot/firmware/config.txt). flycast's JIT crashes (errno 22) on the Pi 5 default 16 KB kernel. A reboot is never automatic: the deploy prints "reboot required". False only stops managing the line; it does not remove one already there. The test VM sets it to false (no Pi firmware, its kernel is already 4 KB).

- Type: `bool`
- Default: `true`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/cabinet_tweaks`

## edition

### `hk_edition`

`community` = nothing under personal/** (no copyrighted art): what a contributor builds. `personal` = also the private overlay (personal/themes). mk/flags.mk reads it from your local file (config/local.yml, else personal/config/local.yml) to pick EDITION before anything else runs; `make EDITION=x` still wins.

- Type: `enum`
- Default: `community`
- Allowed: `personal`, `community`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `mk/flags.mk`

## emulators

### `hk_flycast_resolution`

flycast's internal render height in pixels (emu.cfg rend.Resolution). 0 = follow hk_upscale (480 lines times n: 960 at the default). Set it only to give flycast its own height (480 native, 1440 three times).

- Type: `int`
- Default: `0`
- Range: 0 to 2160
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/dreamcast`

### `hk_flycast_resolution_by_game`

Per-game flycast render height (#179), as {<ROM file name without extension>: <height 240-2160>}, matched without case. flycast-run.sh passes it as a transient `-config config:rend.Resolution=<h>` for that game only (emu.cfg is not touched). Ikaruga runs at native 480 lines: full speed beats sharper pixels on the Pi 5 (the maintainer 2026-11-16). `{}` = every game at hk_flycast_resolution.

- Type: `map`
- Default: `{"Ikaruga": 480}`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/dreamcast`

### `hk_flycast_show_fps`

Draw flycast's frame counter on screen (emu.cfg rend.ShowFPS), top right inside the bezel. Also on while hk_benchmark_mode is.

- Type: `bool`
- Default: `false`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/dreamcast`

### `hk_flycast_vsync`

Wait for the display's vertical sync in flycast (emu.cfg rend.vsync). Off tears but saves a frame of lag.

- Type: `bool`
- Default: `true`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/dreamcast`

### `hk_upscale`

Internal render scale of the 3D systems that can upscale, always 4:3 (#170): PlayStation (PCSX ReARMed enhanced resolution on at 2), N64 (Mupen64Plus-Next 320x240 times n) and Dreamcast/Naomi (flycast 480 lines times n, unless hk_flycast_resolution sets its own). 1 = native, 2 = twice (what the 2 GB Pi 5 holds). 2D systems and Saturn cannot upscale.

- Type: `int`
- Default: `2`
- Range: 1 to 2
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/cabinet_tweaks`, `ansible/roles/dreamcast`

## esde

### `hk_esde_settings`

ES-DE settings written into es_settings.xml, one line per key, in place. Only the keys listed here are accepted (their type is checked); anything else FAILs `make config-check`, so a stray name can never reach the file that holds the ScreenScraper password. Set one key and keep the rest (`hk_esde_settings: {StartupSystem: favorites}`).

- Type: `map`
- Default: `{"CollectionSystemsCustom": "", "CollectionSystemsAuto": "recent", "StartupSystem": "must-play", "CollectionCustomGrouping": "never", "MenuColorScheme": "darkred", "FavoritesAddButton": false, "FavoritesStar": false, "FavoritesFirst": false, "CustomEventScripts": true, "CustomEventScriptsBrowsing": true, "CustomEventScriptsBrowsingNonBlocking": false}`
- Key `CollectionSystemsCustom`: `str`
- Key `CollectionSystemsAuto`: `str`
- Key `StartupSystem`: `str`
- Key `CollectionCustomGrouping`: `str`
- Key `MenuColorScheme`: `str`
- Key `FavoritesAddButton`: `bool`
- Key `FavoritesStar`: `bool`
- Key `FavoritesFirst`: `bool`
- Key `CustomEventScripts`: `bool`
- Key `CustomEventScriptsBrowsing`: `bool`
- Key `CustomEventScriptsBrowsingNonBlocking`: `bool`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/cabinet_tweaks`

## fightcade

### `hk_fightcade_audio_sink`

The PulseAudio sink Fightcade mode (the lobby and FBNeo) plays to, set as PULSE_SINK for those processes only; ES-DE and RetroArch keep the system default. The image's default sink is `combined` (module-combine-sink over both HDMI outputs, skills/build-image/scripts/chroot-setup.sh), whose rate adaptation made FBNeo's audio crackle (#233, cabinet 2026-11-18). `auto` picks the HDMI sink: the only one, or the one whose connector (/sys/class/drm/card*-HDMI-A-N) is connected, matched by its ALSA card vc4-hdmi-(N-1); if that is not exactly one, it keeps the default and logs why. `default` never overrides. Any other value is a sink name from `pactl list short sinks`; one that does not exist keeps the default and logs a warning.

- Type: `str`
- Default: `auto`
- Pattern: `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]*`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/fightcade`
- Example: `alsa_output.platform-107c706400.hdmi.hdmi-stereo`

### `hk_fightcade_binfmt`

Register a binfmt_misc handler (hk-wine, /etc/binfmt.d/coin-dojo-wine.conf) that runs Windows .exe files through Box64 + Wine. Fightcade's lobby starts FBNeo by running its .exe directly, so TEST GAME, TRAINING and every match need it. Any executable .exe on the cabinet then runs under Wine as the user who starts it (never as root: the wrapper refuses). false unregisters the handler and deletes its file on the next deploy; the lobby then cannot start games.

- Type: `bool`
- Default: `true`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/fightcade`

### `hk_fightcade_box64_fast`

Run FBNeo with the Box64 speed flags from #92 (STRONGMEM=0, BIGBLOCK=3, SAFEFLAGS=0, FASTNAN, FASTROUND, CALLRET, FORWARD=1024). Off until the #92 netplay determinism replay test passes: these flags can make the emulation differ from a real x86 PC, and rollback netplay desyncs then. Option B (D3D9, csmt off) reached 59.59 fps on sfiii3 either way.

- Type: `bool`
- Default: `false`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/fightcade`

### `hk_fightcade_chat_macros`

Chat macros of the lobby's on-screen keyboard (#227): one press on the MACROS page types the line into the focused field (START sends it). A list of {group, text}; groups become tabs in order of first use (at most 5, 1-14 capitals/digits/spaces each, no trailing space; MINE is the player's own tab and cannot be used), a line is 1-60 characters without control characters or leading/trailing spaces, 40 lines at most, and both `group` and `text` are required. The defaults are Fightcade's lobby lingo (not verified against Fightcade's own help). Your own list goes in config/local.yml (a deploy and an image build both read it); the macros a player SAVEs on the cabinet are a separate file (/data/fightcade/macros.json) that no deploy writes.

- Type: `list` (items: map)
- Default: `[{"group": "CHALLENGE", "text": "FT2?"}, {"group": "CHALLENGE", "text": "FT3?"}, {"group": "CHALLENGE", "text": "FT5?"}, {"group": "CHALLENGE", "text": "FT10?"}, {"group": "CHALLENGE", "text": "ranked?"}, {"group": "CHALLENGE", "text": "unranked?"}, {"group": "CHALLENGE", "text": "casuals?"}, {"group": "AFTER", "text": "gg"}, {"group": "AFTER", "text": "ggs"}, {"group": "AFTER", "text": "rematch?"}, {"group": "AFTER", "text": "one more?"}, {"group": "AFTER", "text": "ty"}, {"group": "AFTER", "text": "glhf"}, {"group": "STATUS", "text": "brb"}, {"group": "STATUS", "text": "afk"}, {"group": "STATUS", "text": "sorry, lag"}]`
- Key `group`: `str`
- Key `text`: `str`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/fightcade`
- Example: `[{"group": "CHALLENGE", "text": "FT3?"}, {"group": "AFTER", "text": "gg"}]`

### `hk_fightcade_cursor_theme`

Cursor theme of the lobby only (XCURSOR_THEME for Electron), so the stick-as-mouse pointer can be seen. The rest of the cabinet keeps the blank theme. DMZ-White comes from the dmz-cursor-theme package, which the role installs.

- Type: `str`
- Default: `DMZ-White`
- Pattern: `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/fightcade`
- Example: `Adwaita`

### `hk_fightcade_data_dir`

Fightcade's writable data, owned by the cabinet user: the base Wine prefix, the lobby login profile (0700, never copied into images), roms-extra (room clones and the lobby's ROM downloads; ES-DE does not scan it), FBNeo's config folder and logs.

- Type: `path`
- Default: `{{ hk_data_root }}/fightcade`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/fightcade`

### `hk_fightcade_install`

How the third-party Fightcade software (Wine 10.0, Electron 9.1.0, Fightcade 2.1.45, pinned in build/fightcade/pins.json) reaches the cabinet. `deploy`: the deploy (or `make image`) installs it from your own `make -C build fightcade` and builds the Wine prefix. `first-launch` (#267): the deploy or image installs only coin-dojo's own pieces (launcher, Box64, configs) and none of those binaries; the first time the player picks FIGHTCADE, a full-screen consent and progress screen downloads them from their official https URLs (about 292 MiB, sha256-checked), unpacks them and builds the prefix (a few minutes, needs internet and about 2.1 GiB free on the data partition). Use first-launch for an image you hand to other people: it holds no Fightcade binaries.

- Type: `enum`
- Default: `deploy`
- Allowed: `deploy`, `first-launch`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/fightcade`, `skills/build-image/scripts/run.sh`

### `hk_fightcade_install_dir`

Where the Fightcade mode software is unpacked (Box64, Wine 10.0, Electron 9.1.0, Fightcade). Owned by the cabinet user, who unpacks it during the deploy (sha256-checked); root never writes, runs or follows anything there, and the launcher and helpers refuse to run it as root. It needs about 1.3 GB on that filesystem; the deploy refuses a first install with less free. The default is on the data partition: the cabinet's root filesystem is 6.9 GB with ~2.8 GB free (df 2026-11-17), /data ~11 GB free.

- Type: `path`
- Default: `{{ hk_fightcade_data_dir }}/opt`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/fightcade`
- Example: `/opt/coin-dojo/fightcade`

### `hk_image_fightcade`

Put Fightcade mode into the image `make image` builds (#244): Box64 (`make -C build box64`, ~10 min) and the sha256-pinned Wine 10.0, Electron 9.1.0 and Fightcade downloads (`make -C build fightcade`) are installed from your own build folder, and the base Wine prefix is built during the image build; nothing is redistributed. The boot menu then offers FIGHTCADE. Off = an image without Fightcade mode (the boot menu shows only ARCADE); a deploy can add it later. On, the image's data partition is at least 3072 MiB (the install + the Wine prefix need ~2.1 GB). With `hk_fightcade_install: first-launch` (#267) the image holds none of the Wine, Electron or Fightcade files (only Box64 and coin-dojo's own pieces, no build/fightcade needed, no data partition bump): the cabinet downloads them the first time FIGHTCADE is picked.

- Type: `bool`
- Default: `true`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/image.yml`, `skills/build-image/scripts/run.sh`

## guard

### `hk_game_patterns`

Command-line patterns (pgrep -f) for games that run under another process name. The bracket trick (`retroarc[h]`) keeps pgrep from matching its own command line.

- Type: `list` (items: str)
- Default: `["retroarch-1.22/retroarc[h]"]`
- Pattern: `[A-Za-z0-9._/+\[\] -]{1,100}`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `mk/cabinet.mk`, `ansible/roles/esde_common`, `ansible/roles/launcher`
- Also sets the Ansible variable: `esde_game_patterns`

### `hk_game_procs`

Process names (pgrep -x) that mean a game is running. RetroArch and flycast rewrite their files and ES-DE's gamelists on exit, so nothing is written while one runs.

- Type: `list` (items: str)
- Default: `["retroarch", "flycast"]`
- Pattern: `[A-Za-z0-9._+-]{1,15}`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `mk/cabinet.mk`, `ansible/roles/esde_common`, `ansible/roles/launcher`, `ansible/roles/retroarch122`
- Also sets the Ansible variable: `esde_game_procs`

## host

### `hk_become_env`

Environment variable that overrides the Keychain item for the sudo password.

- Type: `str`
- Default: `COIN_DOJO_BECOME_PASS`
- Pattern: `[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/bin/deploy`

### `hk_become_keychain`

Name of the macOS Keychain item that holds the cabinet's sudo password (the value never goes in config).

- Type: `str`
- Default: `coin-dojo-sudo`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/bin/deploy`

### `hk_cabinet_group`

Primary group of the cabinet user.

- Type: `str`
- Default: `{{ hk_cabinet_user }}`
- Pattern: `[a-z_][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/cabinet_tweaks`, `ansible/roles/dreamcast`, `ansible/roles/retroarch122`, `ansible/roles/power`, `ansible/roles/settings`
- Also sets the Ansible variables: `cabinet_group`, `settings_group`

### `hk_cabinet_host`

Address of the cabinet (hostname or IP) that `make deploy`, `make cabinet-guard` and `make smoke-launch` talk to. There is no default on purpose: it is yours. The test VM never uses it.

- Type: `str`
- Default: none, required
- Pattern: `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9.:-]{0,252}`
- Targets: cabinet
- Read by: `mk/cabinet.mk`, `ansible/bin/deploy`, `vm/vm_guard.py`
- Example: `arcade.local`

### `hk_cabinet_uid`

Numeric uid of the cabinet user (the session, flycast, Fightcade and the power daemon use /run/user/<uid>). The first user of a Debian install is 1000; check with `id -u` on your cabinet. make image creates the user with this uid (it removes Pi OS's stock pi, which holds 1000) and stops if they differ.

- Type: `int`
- Default: `1000`
- Range: 1 to 60000
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/power`, `ansible/roles/dreamcast`
- Also sets the Ansible variable: `power_uid`

### `hk_cabinet_user`

The Linux user that runs ES-DE and the games on the cabinet (the image's user).

- Type: `str`
- Default: `coindojo`
- Pattern: `[a-z_][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/cabinet_tweaks`, `ansible/roles/dreamcast`, `ansible/roles/retroarch122`, `ansible/roles/power`, `ansible/roles/settings`, `ansible/roles/sshd_keyonly`
- Also sets the Ansible variables: `cabinet_user`, `settings_user`

### `hk_ssh_common_args`

Extra ssh options for Ansible (ansible_ssh_common_args). Empty for the cabinet.

- Type: `str`
- Default: (empty)
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/bin/deploy`

### `hk_ssh_key`

Private key on this Mac for the cabinet (key auth only; `~` is this Mac's home).

- Type: `path`
- Default: `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `mk/cabinet.mk`, `ansible/bin/ans`

### `hk_ssh_port`

SSH port of the cabinet.

- Type: `int`
- Default: `22`
- Range: 1 to 65535
- Targets: cabinet
- Read by: `ansible/bin/deploy`

### `hk_ssh_user`

SSH login on the cabinet (and on the VM). Follows the cabinet user unless you set it.

- Type: `str`
- Default: `{{ hk_cabinet_user }}`
- Pattern: `[a-z_][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `mk/cabinet.mk`, `ansible/bin/deploy`

### `hk_vm_host`

Address of the test VM as seen from the Ansible container. The lima SSH forward lives on the Mac's loopback, which Colima names host.lima.internal.

- Type: `str`
- Default: `host.lima.internal`
- Pattern: `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9.:-]{0,252}`
- Targets: vm
- Read by: `ansible/bin/deploy`, `vm/vm_guard.py`

### `hk_vm_port`

The Mac port lima forwards to the VM's sshd (vm/coin-dojo-test.yaml ssh.localPort).

- Type: `int`
- Default: `60124`
- Range: 1 to 65535
- Targets: vm
- Read by: `ansible/bin/deploy`, `vm/vm_guard.py`

## launch

### `hk_alt_emulators`

ES-DE per-system default emulator (#47): system -> {label: the ES-DE label from es_systems.xml, core: the libretro core file it needs}. ES-DE 3.5 defaults nes to "Mesen", which is not installed, so NES games would not launch. The deploy asserts every core exists, then pins the label in the system's gamelist (only the `<alternativeEmulator>` block, never `<gameList>`). Dreamcast is pinned by its own role. The test VM has no fbneo core and pins nes only.

- Type: `map`
- Default: `{"nes": {"label": "Nestopia UE", "core": "nestopia_libretro.so"}, "cps1": {"label": "FinalBurn Neo", "core": "fbneo_libretro.so"}, "cps2": {"label": "FinalBurn Neo", "core": "fbneo_libretro.so"}, "cps3": {"label": "FinalBurn Neo", "core": "fbneo_libretro.so"}, "psx": {"label": "PCSX ReARMed", "core": "pcsx_rearmed_libretro.so"}}`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/cabinet_tweaks`

### `hk_benchmark_mode`

Benchmark mode (#185): RetroArch shows its FPS counter top right inside the 4:3 bezel, cyan on a dark backing. RetroArch can draw the counter there only as plain text, so while this is on its popups (achievements included) are plain text in that corner too, without badges. Off = the normal popups. flycast (Dreamcast, Naomi) shows its counter too, top right inside the bezel in the same colours (#187, needs the patched build/flycast, #188).

- Type: `bool`
- Default: `false`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/cabinet_tweaks`, `ansible/roles/dreamcast`

### `hk_core_options`

RetroArch core options, one line each: `{core: <folder under config/>, key: <option>, value: <value>}`, written after the ones hk_upscale derives (PSX enhancement, N64 screen size), so a line here wins. Edited in place (RetroArch rewrites these files with every default, so a whole-file template would fight it).

- Type: `list` (items: map)
- Default: `[{"core": "Flycast", "key": "reicast_internal_resolution", "value": "640x480"}]`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/cabinet_tweaks`

### `hk_retroarch_cfg`

retroarch.cfg keys, one line each: `{key: <name>, value: "<value>"}` (values are quoted strings, as RetroArch writes them). Includes the hotkey and exit buttons; the controls area takes those over later.

- Type: `list` (items: map)
- Default: `[{"key": "input_enable_hotkey_btn", "value": "9"}, {"key": "input_exit_emulator_btn", "value": "8"}, {"key": "input_menu_toggle_btn", "value": "0"}, {"key": "input_overlay_next_btn", "value": "5"}, {"key": "input_pause_toggle_btn", "value": "5"}, {"key": "fps_show", "value": "false"}, {"key": "remap_save_on_exit", "value": "false"}, {"key": "netplay_public_announce", "value": "false"}, {"key": "rgui_aspect_ratio_lock", "value": "0"}, {"key": "cheevos_appearance_anchor", "value": "1"}, {"key": "cheevos_appearance_padding_auto", "value": "true"}, {"key": "menu_show_load_content_animation", "value": "false"}, {"key": "notification_show_config_override_load", "value": "false"}, {"key": "notification_show_autoconfig", "value": "false"}, {"key": "notification_show_autoconfig_fails", "value": "false"}, {"key": "notification_show_remap_load", "value": "false"}, {"key": "video_message_pos_x", "value": "0.160000"}]`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/cabinet_tweaks`

## network

### `hk_net_check_host`

Public host that `make net-check` pings for 60 s next to the cabinet's gateway (avg/max/mdev/loss). An anycast address is close to everyone; pick another if yours filters ICMP.

- Type: `str`
- Default: `1.1.1.1`
- Pattern: `[A-Za-z0-9.:][A-Za-z0-9.:-]{0,252}`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `mk/cabinet.mk`, `tools/net-check.sh`
- Example: `9.9.9.9`

### `hk_wifi_powersave`

Wi-Fi power save on the cabinet. false (or `off`) = OFF for every Wi-Fi network, also ones joined later in the SETTINGS app: a NetworkManager drop-in (/etc/NetworkManager/conf.d/90-coin-dojo-wifi.conf, `wifi.powersave = 2`). Power save made pings jitter and drop (2026-11-18, 60 s to a public host: 7.5 % loss, mdev 29.8 ms with it on; 0 % and 8.1 ms off), and rollback netcode turns that into stutter. The cabinet runs on mains power, so off costs nothing. true (or `on`) removes the drop-in: back to the NetworkManager/driver default. A change applies at the next reconnect of each Wi-Fi network; the deploy says when one still has power save on.

- Type: `bool`
- Default: `false`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/cabinet_tweaks`

### `hk_wifi_reconnect_polkit`

Let the cabinet user run NetworkManager network-control from any session, SSH included, without sudo: one polkit rule (/etc/polkit-1/rules.d/51-coin-dojo-net.rules), that one action only. Needed to apply a Wi-Fi change such as the power save above over SSH (a reconnect). Its real scope: bring any SAVED connection up or down (also another saved network), disconnect a device or set it unmanaged (over Wi-Fi SSH that locks you out until you fix it at the cabinet or reboot), and change a device at runtime (IP, DNS, routes; not saved). It does NOT create, change or save connections. The SETTINGS app's own rule (role settings) covers only the cabinet's seat. false removes the rule.

- Type: `bool`
- Default: `true`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/cabinet_tweaks`

Root of the nested ROM tree the main-screen collections point ES-DE at (es_systems.xml <path>).

Where the ROMs live (one folder per system).

The collections workspace on the cabinet (tools, picks, dat, folder art, nested_out).

## power

### `hk_power_nice`

Scheduler priority (nice) of the power daemon; negative keeps the button responsive while an emulator keeps the cores busy.

- Type: `int`
- Default: `-5`
- Range: -20 to 19
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/power`

### `hk_power_prompt`

Seconds the "Shut down?" prompt waits for the second press before it cancels (also the countdown the prompt shows).

- Type: `int`
- Default: `8`
- Range: 3 to 30
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/power`

### `hk_power_stop_timeout`

Longest a single process may take to stop during shutdown (systemd DefaultTimeoutStopSec and the user manager's TimeoutStopSec). The distro default is 90 s. Keep it between 10 s and 30 s: shorter can cut a save in progress, longer feels hung.

- Type: `str`
- Default: `15s`
- Pattern: `[0-9]+(s|min)`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/power`

## session

### `hk_session_countdown`

Seconds the boot menu waits at power-on before it starts ARCADE (ES-DE) by itself; any input stops the countdown. 0 = always wait for a choice. After a mode ends the menu always waits.

- Type: `int`
- Default: `5`
- Range: 0 to 60
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/session`

### `hk_session_enable`

Run the session loop (coin-dojo-session) on tty1 instead of plain ES-DE. false puts the plain `exec cage -d -- es-de ...` line back into ~/.bash_profile on the next deploy (the rollback); it takes effect at the next login on tty1 (reboot).

- Type: `bool`
- Default: `true`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/session`

## settings

### `hk_cabinet_hostname`

The cabinet's name on the network (`<name>.local`, also the network folder's address, #266), one RFC 1123 label: a-z, 0-9 and `-`, 1 to 63 characters, no `-` at either end. `make image` names the image with it. The SETTINGS app lets you rename the cabinet; this is the name the preview and the VM show.

- Type: `str`
- Default: `coindojo`
- Pattern: `[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `skills/settings/Makefile`

### `hk_settings_helper_dest`

Where the root helper that renames the cabinet is installed. The sudoers line allows the cabinet user to run exactly this path with one valid name.

- Type: `path`
- Default: `/usr/local/sbin/coin-dojo-set-hostname`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/settings`

### `hk_settings_nmcli`

The NetworkManager command line tool the SETTINGS app calls for Wi-Fi (a name on PATH or an absolute path).

- Type: `str`
- Default: `nmcli`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/settings`

### `hk_settings_polkit`

Install the NetworkManager polkit rule that lets the cabinet user scan, connect and save Wi-Fi at the cabinet's own seat. The test VM has no NetworkManager and switches it off in ansible/inventory/vm.yml.

- Type: `bool`
- Default: `true`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/settings`

### `hk_timezone`

The cabinet's time zone (`timedatectl list-timezones`, e.g. `Europe/Berlin`). The settings role applies it with `timedatectl set-timezone` only when the cabinet has none of its own: a zone picked on the cabinet (SETTINGS, TIME ZONE) is kept in the state file and wins over this value on every deploy. Set yours in your local config.

- Type: `str`
- Default: `Etc/UTC`
- Pattern: `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_+-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_+-]*){0,2}`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/settings`

## shaders

### `hk_crt_enabled`

Apply the CRT shader to RetroArch systems. true: RetroArch's auto shader presets are on and the shader files and presets are installed. false: the two RetroArch switches (auto_shaders_enable, video_shader_enable) are set to false and nothing shader-related is installed (files already on the cabinet are left alone).

- Type: `bool`
- Default: `true`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/retroarch122`

### `hk_crt_off_cores`

Cores that get the plain pass-through instead of the CRT preset (upscaled 3D looks wrong under scanlines: the N64 and PSX cores render at 2x to 3x). Names are RetroArch's library_name, the same as the folders under ~/.config/retroarch/config, remaps and core-options. `[]` puts scanlines on every core.

- Type: `list` (items: enum)
- Default: `["Mupen64Plus-Next", "PCSX-ReARMed"]`
- Allowed: `Beetle PCE`, `Beetle Saturn`, `FinalBurn Neo`, `Flycast`, `Genesis Plus GX`, `MAME`, `Mupen64Plus-Next`, `Nestopia`, `PCSX-ReARMed`, `Snes9x`, `Stella`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/retroarch122`

### `hk_crt_preset`

The preset every RetroArch system gets (config/global.glslp points at it). crt-pi is the cheap scanline shader that runs full speed on the Pi 5. Only presets the role pins (sha256) are allowed; another preset needs its files added to retroarch122_shader_files first.

- Type: `enum`
- Default: `crt/crt-pi.glslp`
- Allowed: `crt/crt-pi.glslp`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/retroarch122`

## share

### `hk_share_bios_veto`

Names the network folder hides and refuses in the `bios` share (Samba `veto files`, any depth): folders or files emulators read SCRIPTS or settings from, which the network folder must not be able to plant. `mame` = the MAME core's whole system subtree (`bios/mame/`: ini files, which can name an autoboot Lua script, plugins, Lua, cheats, hash files); `*.lua` = any Lua script. Normal BIOS files (zip, bin, rom, pce) still copy. Copy MAME's own files over SSH if you need them. One name or shell pattern per item, no `/`. Empty: nothing blocked.

- Type: `list` (items: str)
- Default: `["mame", "*.lua"]`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/share`
- Example: `[mame, "*.lua", fbneo]`

### `hk_share_enable`

Share exactly two folders on the home network: `roms` (hk_rom_root) and `bios` (hk_bios_root), as `smb://<name>.local` (Finder) and `\\<name>.local` (Windows Explorer). Login: the cabinet user and its network password (the community image sets the default login's password; SETTINGS > PASSWORD changes the login and this password together). SMB3 only, no guest, LAN interfaces and private addresses only, nothing else shared (no home folders, no printers). Installs Samba and avahi (mDNS, `<name>.local`) from Debian. true in the community edition; the personal edition turns it off in its local config. false stops and disables Samba and removes the folder's mDNS entry (the packages stay).

- Type: `bool`
- Default: `true`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/share`

### `hk_share_roms_veto`

Names the network folder hides and refuses in the `roms` share (Samba `veto files`, any depth, renames included): `*.cmd` = MAME command files (they can name an `-autoboot_script` Lua script), `*.lua` = Lua scripts, `mame` = a folder named like MAME's settings tree. ROM folders (`roms/arcade`, `roms/fbneo` ...) and every ROM extension the cabinet's systems use stay open (no system uses .cmd). One name or shell pattern per item, no `/`. Empty: nothing blocked.

- Type: `list` (items: str)
- Default: `["mame", "*.lua", "*.cmd"]`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/share`
- Example: `[mame, "*.lua", "*.cmd"]`

## storage

### `hk_journal_keep_free`

Free space journald leaves on the root filesystem (SystemKeepFree=); it stops growing below this. Keep it under what your card has free, or the cap shrinks to nothing and the previous boot is vacuumed away.

- Type: `str`
- Default: `500M`
- Pattern: `[1-9][0-9]*[KMGT]`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/journald`
- Example: `1G`

### `hk_journal_max_use`

Most disk the systemd journal may use (journald SystemMaxUse=). A number and a unit K, M, G or T. 50M holds many boots of the cabinet (a boot is about 5M) and spares the SD card.

- Type: `str`
- Default: `50M`
- Pattern: `[1-9][0-9]*[KMGT]`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/journald`
- Example: `100M`

### `hk_journal_retention`

Drop journal entries older than this even when under the size cap (MaxRetentionSec=). A number and one of s, m, h, d, w, month, year.

- Type: `str`
- Default: `1month`
- Pattern: `[1-9][0-9]*(s|m|h|d|w|month|year)`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/journald`
- Example: `2week`

### `hk_purge_groups`

Package groups the diskhygiene role removes (apt purge) on a deploy that applies. The groups are defined in the role (toolchain, firmware_other_chips, mkvtoolnix, rpi_connect); each one is simulated first and the plan fails when it would remove more than it lists or a protected package. Empty: plan and report only.

- Type: `list` (items: str)
- Default: `["toolchain"]`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/diskhygiene`
- Example: `[toolchain, mkvtoolnix]`

### `hk_swap`

Swap of the cabinet (Raspberry Pi OS rpi-swap + systemd-zram-generator). mechanism: zram is RAM only, with no swap file on the SD card; zram+file adds a writeback file on the card; auto leaves it to the distro. ram_multiplier: zram size as a multiple of RAM. max_mib: cap of the zram device in MiB (2048 shows as 1.9G on a 2 GB Pi 5). Set one key and keep the rest (`hk_swap: {max_mib: 1024}`).

- Type: `map`
- Default: `{"mechanism": "zram", "ram_multiplier": 1, "max_mib": 2048}`
- Key `mechanism`: `enum`
- Key `ram_multiplier`: `float`, 0.1 to 4
- Key `max_mib`: `int`, 64 to 65536
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/cabinet_tweaks`

### `hk_theme_keep`

The one ES-DE theme folder on the cabinet that diskhygiene never removes. Follows the active theme; the role refuses to run when it is on its removal list.

- Type: `str`
- Default: `{{ hk_theme_name }}`
- Pattern: `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/diskhygiene`

### `hk_vm_swappiness`

Kernel vm.swappiness, set permanently in /etc/sysctl.d/99-zz-coin-dojo.conf (#209; sorts after 98-rpi.conf). 1 = swap only under real memory pressure: it removed a 144 ms swap-in hitch in the Fightcade run (#92) and keeps ES-DE in RAM too. The Debian default is 60.

- Type: `int`
- Default: `1`
- Range: 0 to 200
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/session`

## theme

### `hk_eye_glow`

The slow glow over the eyes of the backdrop (skills/badges/gen_eye_glow.py). enabled: draw it at all; peak: strongest opacity of the loop, 0 to 1; box: x0, y0, x1, y1 of the glow in backdrop pixels (1440x1080), around the eyes of YOUR art. Set one key and keep the rest (`hk_eye_glow: {peak: 0.6}`).

- Type: `map`
- Default: `{"enabled": true, "peak": 0.92, "box": [680, 85, 960, 345]}`
- Key `enabled`: `bool`
- Key `peak`: `float`, 0.0 to 1.0
- Key `box`: `list`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `skills/badges/gen_eye_glow.py`, `ansible/roles/esde_theme`
- Also sets the Ansible variable: `esde_theme_eye_glow`

### `hk_hotkey_strip`

Show the small hotkey badge strip above the footer on game lists.

- Type: `bool`
- Default: `true`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/esde_theme`
- Also sets the Ansible variable: `esde_theme_hotkey_strip`

### `hk_rev_stamp`

Show the REV build stamp (git describe) bottom-left in the footer.

- Type: `bool`
- Default: `true`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/esde_theme`
- Also sets the Ansible variable: `esde_theme_rev_stamp`

### `hk_theme_art_dir`

Your own art folder, laid over the theme at deploy: backdrops/default.png (1440x1080 PNG) and an optional backdrops/<system>.png per system (plus eye-glow.* when you have them). Relative paths start at the repo root. Unset: the theme shows its own backdrop, the night art (backdrops/default.png) with its eye glow; the dojo (backdrops/dojo.png, gen_backdrop.py) is the alternative. The art never leaves this folder (it is not committed or copied elsewhere).

- Type: `str`
- Default: (empty)
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/esde_theme`, `skills/badges/gen_eye_glow.py`
- Also sets the Ansible variable: `esde_theme_art_dir`
- Example: `personal/themes/coin-dojo/_inc/art`

### `hk_theme_name`

Folder name of the ES-DE theme under themes/ (and under ~/ES-DE/themes on the cabinet).

- Type: `str`
- Default: `coin-dojo`
- Pattern: `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/esde_theme`
- Also sets the Ansible variable: `esde_theme_name`

### `hk_theme_overlay`

Lay the personal overlay (personal/themes/<theme>) over the theme at deploy. EDITION=community never does, whatever this says. Set false to deploy the repo theme alone.

- Type: `bool`
- Default: `true`
- Targets: cabinet, vm
- Read by: `ansible/roles/esde_theme`
- Also sets the Ansible variable: `esde_theme_personal`
